What is the purpose of this hook ? @HomePage.tsx (15-26) 

Why is this needed as opposed to just regular tailwind css classes that match media queries with e.g `max-md:` or `min-sm` ? Just answer
</user_query>
The hook is there so the map is only created for the layout that’s actually on screen. I’ll confirm that against the page before answering.

The `explain` skill is for Linear issues, so it does not apply here.

`useMdUp` decides which layout is mounted. Tailwind classes like `hidden md:block` only hide elements; both copies stay in the DOM. Leaflet measures its container when `ParkMap` first mounts, and a `display: none` container is 0px tall, so the map stays blank after the class later shows it. The hook mounts the desktop map or the phone layout, never both, and switches when the window crosses 768px.

I didn't see the whole implementation before I started tearing it apart. This makes sense. Should this MD_QUERY reference a tailwind design system breakpoint rather than redeclare it?
const MD_QUERY = '(min-width: 48rem)'

</user_query>
`matchMedia` cannot see a Tailwind class, so the question is whether `48rem` should be read from the theme instead of written out again. I’ll check how this project defines `md`.

Keep `MD_QUERY` as the literal `(min-width: 48rem)`.

This project’s theme only defines colors. `src/index.css` says `md` stays at Tailwind’s default, which is `--breakpoint-md: 48rem` in Tailwind’s theme. There is no design-system breakpoint token to import.

`window.matchMedia` needs a full query string. It cannot use the `md:` variant or `var(--breakpoint-md)`, because custom properties are invalid inside a media query. `(min-width: 48rem)` is the same threshold Tailwind uses for `md:` (`width >= 48rem`).

That string would need a matching edit only if someone later changed `--breakpoint-md` in `@theme`. This app keeps that value fixed.
